title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(廣田哲夫研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Hirota Tetsuo)
educationalGoal: Students will acquire engineering problem-finding, solving, and application skills related to knowledge and skills in the information and communication field, which are highly important in modern society. To this end, students develop engineering skills such as design ability, ability to analyze experimental results, logical thinking ability, and communication ability through research on project themes. If necessary, they will review the basic subjects and review the literature.
advice: Based on the contents learned in the “Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III” in the 3rd year, each has its own project theme and is active as a group or alone. This course is the final subject of a series of project design education, and is positioned as a subject that integrates the items learned in all subjects. Aim to review basic subjects and acquire advanced expertise through activities. The annual schedule is as follows. [First half of the 4th year] Understand related research contents conducted in the past, and learn circuit design methods, how to use design tools, and circuit fabrication methods. Make an interim presentation at the end of the semester. [Second half of the 4th year] At the end of the semester, the results will be compiled into a project report and presented at the presentation screening meeting. If necessary, take over to the next year's student. Project themes include: (1) Microwave digital phase shifter (2) Microwave variable output amplifier (3) Microwave power distributor Details are shown separately.
requiredKnowledge: It is required to vigorously learn basic knowledge, identify problems, and plan solutions to problems themselves. It is necessary to have the ability to review the progress so far and to find a better direction through discussions with supervisors, graduate students, and classmates. It is also necessary to always learn the habit of recording the activity and learning contents so that they can be used later.

activityGoals.body: Be able to clarify the purpose of the project, understand the contents, and draw up a research plan
Be able to materialize and implement problems in project execution and solutions to problems
Be able to communicate well with project members and faculty members and evaluate activity results correctly
Be able to summarize activity results in a project report
Be able to explain the contents of the project and present the results of activities effectively

achievementLevels.ideal: After understanding the significance and purpose of the project, be able to formulate and plan solutions to the project's goals yourself, achieve the goals, summarize the results in appropriate reports, and make effective presentations.
achievementLevels.standard: Be able to understand the significance and purpose of the project, work systematically toward the goal, almost achieve the goal, summarize the results in an appropriate report, and give a presentation.

lessons.content: Seminars are conducted every week. Students are required to report on the contents of the activities and discuss how to proceed later. They are also required to prepare for a presentation at the Design Project III Public Presentation Review Meeting and prepare a project report.
